purpose: Evaluate an independent background-light overlap screen; no live promotion

screen.missing_reference: withhold; do not invent a background signal
screen.channels: All three background RGB channels independently; unchanged PulseTrace green-channel filter/PSD path for each
screen.action: Withhold a candidate if any background channel has enough band power near that candidate; no frequency replacement or reference-rate input

scoring: Separate pulse-present accepted-set error, all-case coverage, correct readings retained/lost (within 5 BPM), wrong readings retained/removed, and no-pulse spurious-candidate counts. Break down by reference mode. Preserve all raw estimates and no-reference baselines.
selection: Full pulse-present Cartesian grid plus controls without redundant pulse direction; every face input shared across methods and reference modes. Reference includes no physiological pulse except deliberately invalid pulse_leakage cases. Rate 138 deliberately coincides with colored light to measure rejection of real pulse.
limitations: Research RGB-level model, not video or natural validation. Background response differs from face response. Shared illumination is an assumption; face-only interference and pulse contamination deliberately violate it. A frequency match is ambiguity, not proof of lighting; no overlap is not proof of pulse. Missing archived backgrounds cannot be reconstructed from facial measurements.
